claim: Type-constrained decoding uses novel prefix automata and a search over inhabitable types to enforce well-typedness on LLM-generated code at every decoding step, reducing compilation errors by more than half on HumanEval and MBPP.
scope_conditions: HumanEval, MBPP; simply-typed calculus formalization extended to TypeScript; model sizes up to 30B+; ACM PACMPL/OOPSLA 2025
quoted_support: Our evaluation on the HumanEval and MBPP datasets shows that our approach reduces compilation errors by more than half and significantly increases functional correctness in code synthesis, translation, and repair tasks across LLMs of various sizes and model families.
numbers: compilation errors reduced by more than half

claim: Constrained decoding for general-purpose programming languages has so far only been applied to domain-specific languages or syntactic/type-system features, not to dynamic, natural-language-specified behavioral requirements.
stance_target: novelty of confidence-triggered, requirement-level decoding (candidate a)
scope_conditions: constrained decoding literature as of Apr 2025
quoted_support: Although constrained decoding is a promising approach to alleviate this issue, it has only been applied to handle either domain-specific languages or syntactic features of general-purpose programming languages.

claim: LLMs frequently generate code with typing errors that are beyond the domain of syntax and generally hard to adequately constrain, motivating a formal type-system-guided decoding approach.
quoted_support: LLMs frequently generate code with typing errors, which are beyond the domain of syntax and generally hard to adequately constrain.
